questions.question: Q1. In the SBA dashboard, what is the purpose of the NF tile?

answers.b: To select and configure a Network Function

explanations.a: Incorrect — UE information is not shown on NF tiles.
explanations.b: Correct — NF tiles are used to select, configure, and start specific NFs.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Bandwidth usage is not displayed on NF tiles.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Dashboard reset is a separate function.

questions.question: Q2. What information must be entered before starting an NF manually?

answers.b: IP Address, Port Number, and Protocol

explanations.a: Incorrect — UE information is unrelated to NF configuration.
explanations.b: Correct — Every NF requires IP, port, and protocol before starting.
explanations.c: Incorrect — PLMN/TAC are used for RAN, not NF deployment.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Database credentials are not required here.

questions.question: Q3. During manual deployment, how does the system indicate that an NF is ready?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Red indicates error, not readiness.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Freezing indicates a system issue.
explanations.c: Correct — The Logs Panel displays 'NF ready' or similar messages.
explanations.d: Incorrect — No popup is shown for readiness.

questions.question: Q4. In one-click deployment, what is the first internal step performed by the system?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Deployment happens after topology cleanup.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Connections are established only after NFs launch.
explanations.c: Correct — The system first clears old or running NFs.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Ping tests are done manually by the user.

questions.question: Q5. During automated core deployment, which step ensures NF-to-NF connectivity?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Config loading does not establish connectivity.
explanations.b: Correct — Internal SBA connections are automatically created between NFs.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Terminal checks are manual validation steps.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Port reassignment does not link NFs.

questions.question: Q6. What message typically confirms that the AMF has successfully launched in the logs panel?

explanations.b: Correct — This message confirms a successful AMF startup.
explanations.c: Incorrect — This indicates a link loss.
explanations.d: Incorrect — This is an error message.

questions.question: Q7. Why is stabilization time (4–5 seconds) required after starting an NF?

answers.b: To allocate memory and initialize internal components

explanations.a: Incorrect — Protocol upgrades are not automatic.
explanations.b: Correct — NFs need a few seconds to initialize their internal modules.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Authentication keys are not generated here.

questions.question: Q8. What does the “Core Deploy” button do in one-click deployment?

answers.b: Automatically launches and interconnects all NFs

explanations.a: Incorrect — IPs are part of configuration, not deployment.
explanations.b: Correct — It initiates automated deployment of all NFs at once.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Ping must be executed manually.
explanations.d: Incorrect — It does not open config files.

questions.question: Q9. Which panel is used to observe 'NRF registration completed' logs?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Topology shows NF layout, not logs.
explanations.b: Correct — Logs Panel displays all NF registration and status logs.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Terminal is for command execution.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Metrics panel shows performance data.

questions.question: Q10. After opening the NF terminal, which detail is displayed at the top?

explanations.a: Incorrect — UE details are not shown in NF terminal.
explanations.b: Correct — The terminal header displays NF name and its assigned IP.
explanations.c: Incorrect — NRF status is not shown here.
explanations.d: Incorrect — CPU metrics are found in performance panels, not terminal.

questions.question: Q11. What does a successful ping test between NFs indicate?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Wrong values would result in ping failures.
explanations.b: Correct — Ping success means NFs can reach each other.
explanations.c: Incorrect — CPU load does not impact ping results directly.
explanations.d: Incorrect — PLMN IDs are unrelated to NF connectivity.

questions.question: Q12. Which result represents a perfect NF connectivity test?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Any packet loss indicates connection issues.
explanations.c: Correct — 0% packet loss confirms strong connectivity.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Missing logs do not indicate connectivity.

questions.question: Q13. What action does the dashboard perform before launching all NFs in one-click mode?

explanations.b: Correct — The system resets or clears older NFs before deployment.
explanations.c: Incorrect — User profile creation is unrelated to core deployment.
explanations.d: Incorrect — IPs are not reset automatically.

questions.question: Q14. What happens when you start an NF without selecting a protocol?

explanations.b: Correct — Missing protocol results in NF startup failure.
explanations.c: Incorrect — The system never switches to 4G automatically.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Logs remain open regardless of protocol selection.

questions.question: Q15. Which NF action cannot be performed during stabilization time?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Logs can be viewed anytime.
explanations.b: Correct — IP cannot be modified while NF is stabilizing.
explanations.c: Incorrect — You can start other NFs independently.
